title: gmx-schema v1
description:
The open, on-disk project format for GameMaker eXperimental.
Each top-level resource kind has a definition under `$defs`; per-file schema hints reference one with `#<kind>`.

oneOf.description: A normal playable game project.
A project template that the IDE can clone when creating a new project.

TemplateKind.description:
Whether this project is a standalone game or a reusable project template.
Templates appear in the GameMaker IDE's "New Project" dialog for cloning.

order.description:
Room names in play order. The first entry is the room the
game opens with. Names must match folders under `rooms/`.

RoomOrder.description: Order in which the game's rooms are entered at startup.

order.description:
Resource names in the order they should appear in the build
output. Anything not listed here falls through to the default
alphabetical order at the end.

ResourceOrder.description:
Explicit ordering of asset resources for the build output.
When omitted or empty, resources are emitted alphabetically by
kind.

draw_colour.description:
Background colour the engine clears the screen to before
drawing each frame. `"#RRGGBB"` hex format. Defaults to
`"#FFFFFF"` (white).

window_colour.description:
Colour shown around the game view when the view doesn't
fill the OS window. `"#RRGGBB"` hex. Defaults to `"#FF0000"`
(red).

game_speed.description:
Target frame rate in frames per second, as used by
`game_set_speed(n, gamespeed_fps)`.

gameid.description:
Numeric game identifier used by GameMaker's marketplace and
platform services. Leave at `0` if you're not publishing.

gameguid.description:
Stable globally-unique identifier for this game. Generated
once and preserved across builds; platform stores use it to
recognise the title.

author.description:
Author name embedded in build metadata and readable at runtime
via platform-specific game-info APIs.

flags.description: Engine behaviour toggles (compatibility flags, build options).

mips_for_3d_textures.description:
Generate mipmaps for 3D textures at build time. Slightly larger
output, smoother minification when textures are sampled from a
distance.

sci_usesci.description:
Enable Source Code Inspection (SCI) — additional runtime
metadata that lets debug builds attribute crashes back to
source positions.

spine_licence.description:
Embed a Spine runtime licence acknowledgment in the build.
Required only if the project uses Spine-animated sprites.

steam_app_id.description:
Steamworks application ID (`steam_appid.txt`). Leave at `0`
if not publishing on Steam.

template_description.description:
Human-readable description of the project template (only
meaningful if this project is itself published as a
template).

template_icon.description:
Path to a PNG used as the template's thumbnail icon when this
project is published as a template.

template_image.description:
Path to a PNG used as the template's preview image when this
project is published as a template.

GameSettings.description:
Game-wide settings: window colours, frame rate, identifiers,
engine compatibility flags.

allow_instance_change.description:
Allow changing an instance's object via `instance_change()`
in contexts where older runtimes rejected it.

copy_on_write_enabled.description:
Enable copy-on-write semantics for arrays and structs; kept off
for compatibility with older projects.

start_fullscreen.description:
Start the game in fullscreen mode on every platform. Acts as a
default: a per-platform `start_fullscreen` value (in
`options/<platform>.toml`) takes precedence.

allow_fullscreen.description:
Allow the player to toggle fullscreen at runtime on every
platform. Acts as a default: a per-platform `allow_fullscreen`
value takes precedence.

resize_window.description:
Allow the player to resize the game window at runtime on every
platform. Acts as a default: a per-platform `resize_window`
value takes precedence.

display_cursor.description:
Show the OS cursor over the game window on every platform. Acts
as a default: a per-platform `display_cursor` value takes
precedence.

remove_unused_assets.description:
Strip assets that aren't referenced by any code or room from
the build output. Turn this off if you need the final build
to contain every asset in the project.

GameFlags.description:
Engine behaviour toggles that affect runtime semantics and build
output.

link.description:
Folder name under `prefabs/` that contains this prefab's
assets; must match the actual directory name on disk.

name.description:
Human-readable label for this prefab. Typically the same as
`link`.

path.description:
Path to the prefab's GameMaker project file, relative to its
`prefabs/<link>/` directory.

PrefabRef.description:
Reference to a prefab this project includes. An explicit entry
fixes the merge order for that prefab; the on-disk folder name
must match `link`.

min_version.description:
Minimum runner version this project needs. Free-form string
(semver-like, build ID, etc.). `gmx run` reads this to decide
which runner to launch; today it surfaces a notice when set.
Omit for projects that work on any runner build.

Runner.description:
Runtime requirements declared by `project.toml`. Currently a single
`min_version` hint; future fields can declare specific feature
requirements or pin a runner build.

schema_version.description:
Format version of this project file. Currently always `1` and
can be omitted; reserved for future incompatible changes.

name.description:
Display name of the project. Used in window titles and
platform manifests at build time.

template.description:
Whether this is a regular game or a template that the IDE
can clone to create new projects.

ecma.description:
Run the project under ECMAScript-compatible numeric semantics.
Leave off unless you specifically need that compatibility mode.

room_order.description:
Order rooms are visited when the game starts. The first
room in `order` is the one that runs first.

resource_order.description:
Explicit ordering of asset resources for the build output.
Optional — when omitted, assets are emitted in alphabetical
order grouped by kind. Set this only when you need to
preserve a specific iteration order.

game.description:
Game-wide settings (window, draw colours, frame rate, GUIDs,
engine flags).

prefabs.description:
Prefab packages this project depends on. Each entry controls
merge order for the corresponding `prefabs/<link>/` directory;
any `prefabs/` subdirectory not listed here is auto-discovered
and appended alphabetically at build time.

texture_group_order.description:
Explicit ordering of texture groups. The texture packer
processes groups in this order, which affects which sprites
end up on which atlas page. Optional — alphabetical when
omitted.

audio_group_order.description:
Explicit ordering of audio groups (the `.yyp`'s declaration order,
with `audiogroup_default` at index 0). The AGRP chunk and audio-group
string indices follow this order. Optional — alphabetical when omitted.

runner.description:
Runtime requirements for this project. Lets `gmx run` resolve
the right runner binary (or warn when the available runner is
too old to support the features the project uses).

constants.description:
Arbitrary project-wide constants, referenceable from GML as
`project::constants.<key>` and resolved to literals at build time
by the toml-ref pass. Lives under its own table so
`deny_unknown_fields` still protects the rest of `project.toml`.

project.description:
Top-level project metadata. Lives at the project root as
`project.toml`.
project.title: Project

oneOf.description: Preserve the aspect ratio, letterboxing as needed.
Stretch to fill the whole surface, ignoring aspect ratio.

WindowScale.description: How the game surface scales to fill the window/canvas.

display_name.description:
The game's display name shown in the title bar, Dock, and macOS app switcher.
Required — no meaningful default exists; this is project-specific.

app_id.description:
The reverse-DNS bundle identifier (e.g. `"com.example.mygame"`), used by macOS to
uniquely identify the app.

version.description:
Four-part version string (`major.minor.patch.build`, e.g. `"1.0.0.0"`).
Exposed at runtime as `GM_version`.

build_number.description:
Monotonically increasing build number used by the App Store to distinguish
submissions with the same version string.

interpolate_pixels.description: When `true`, textures are scaled with bilinear filtering instead of nearest-neighbour.

display_cursor.description:
When `true`, the OS mouse cursor is visible over the game window.
`None` inherits the project's `game.flags.display_cursor` engine
flag; a value here overrides it.

start_fullscreen.description:
Start the game in fullscreen mode. `None` inherits the project's
`game.flags.start_fullscreen` engine flag; a value here overrides it.

allow_fullscreen.description:
Allow the player to toggle fullscreen at runtime. `None` inherits the
project's `game.flags.allow_fullscreen` engine flag; a value here overrides it.

resize_window.description:
Allow the player to resize the game window at runtime. `None` inherits the
project's `game.flags.resize_window` engine flag; a value here overrides it.

vsync.description: Synchronise frame presentation to the display refresh rate to prevent tearing.

arm64.description: Include an Apple Silicon (arm64) slice in the app bundle.

x86_64.description: Include an Intel (x86_64) slice in the app bundle.

team_id.description:
Apple Developer Team ID used for code-signing (e.g. `"ABCDE12345"`).
Required for distribution outside the Mac App Store. Leave empty to sign ad-hoc.

signing_identity.description:
Code-signing identity name as it appears in Keychain
(e.g. `"Developer ID Application: My Company (ABCDE12345)"`).

copyright.description: Copyright string embedded in the app's `Info.plist` (e.g. `"© 2024 My Company"`).

icon_png.description:
Path to a PNG file used as the application icon (1024×1024 recommended).
Relative to the project root.

splash_png.description:
Path to a PNG file shown as the loading/splash screen before the first room loads.
Relative to the project root.

installer_background_png.description:
Path to a PNG image used as the background of the macOS PKG installer.
Relative to the project root.

allow_incoming_network.description:
Allow the game to accept incoming network connections (e.g. for hosted multiplayer).
Adds the matching network-server entitlement to the bundle.

allow_outgoing_network.description:
Allow the game to initiate outgoing network connections (e.g. HTTP requests, telemetry).
Adds the matching network-client entitlement to the bundle.

apple_sign_in.description:
Enable the Sign in with Apple capability for the bundle. Required if the game uses
Apple ID authentication.

app_category.description:
LSApplicationCategoryType embedded in `Info.plist`. Affects categorisation in the
Mac App Store.

build_app_store.description:
Build a Mac App Store-flavoured bundle (sandboxed, receipt-validated) instead of a
Developer-ID-signed standalone bundle.

disable_sandbox.description:
Disable the App Sandbox entitlement. Required for some Steam features; rejected
by the Mac App Store.

enable_steam.description: Link against the Steamworks SDK and enable Steam-specific features at runtime.

menu_dock.description:
Show the macOS menu bar and Dock icon while the game is running. When `false`, the
game runs as a full-screen kiosk-style app.

output_dir.description:
Default output directory the IDE writes built bundles to. Local to the user's
machine; not used at runtime.

texture_page.description: Maximum texture page size used by the macOS packer (e.g. `"2048x2048"`).

display_cursor.description: When `true`, the OS mouse cursor is visible over the game canvas.

edit_url.description: URL the player is sent to when editing the game's listing on GX.games.

game_name.description:
Display name shown on the game's GX.games listing. Supports the `${project_name}`
placeholder.

guid.description: Stable GX.games identifier for the published game. Assigned when the listing is created.

internal_share_url.description: Internal share URL used by the publisher while the listing is private.

mod_edit_url.description: Edit URL for the mod listing on GX.games.

mod_guid.description: Stable GX.games identifier for the published mod.

mod_internal_share_url.description: Internal share URL for the mod listing while private.

mod_public_share_url.description: Public share URL for the mod listing once it goes live.

mod_team_name.description: Display name of the team that owns the mod listing.

public_share_url.description: Public share URL for the game listing once it goes live.

team_name.description: Display name of the team that owns the game listing.

transparent_background.description:
When `true`, the GX.games canvas renders with a transparent background, letting
the surrounding page show through.

Relative to the project root.

splash_png.description:

Relative to the project root.

installer_finished_png.description:
Path to a BMP shown on the installer's "finished" page.
Relative to the project root.

installer_header_png.description:
Path to a BMP shown as the installer's header banner.
Relative to the project root.

borderless.description: Run the game in a borderless window (no title bar, no resize grip).

copy_exe_to_dest.description:
After building, copy the resulting EXE next to the project file. Useful for some
CI / distribution workflows.

d3d_swap_effect_discard.description:
Use `DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_DISCARD` when presenting the D3D11 swapchain. Required for
compatibility on older Windows configurations; modern Windows uses
`DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_FLIP_DISCARD` when `false`.

disable_sandbox.description:
Disable the sandboxed file-access path. Required for some Steam features; weakens
the security model.

enable_steam.description: Link against the Steamworks SDK and enable Steam-specific features at runtime.

executable_name.description:
Filename of the produced EXE, e.g. `"mygame.exe"`. When empty, the
project name + `.exe` is used at build time.

license.description:
Path to a plain-text licence agreement shown by the installer.
Relative to the project root.

nsis_file.description:
Path to a custom NSIS installer script. Relative to the project root.
When omitted, the IDE generates a default script.

save_location.description:
Where the game stores its save files: `"app_data"` (`%LOCALAPPDATA%`)
or `"next_to_exe"`.

sleep_margin.description:
Per-frame sleep margin (milliseconds) used by the frame limiter when targeting a
fixed game speed. Lower values reduce frame jitter at the cost of more CPU.

steam_use_alternative_launcher.description:
Use the alternative Steam launcher (separate `.exe` that launches the main binary).
Improves compatibility with the Steam overlay on some setups.

texture_page.description: Maximum texture page size used by the Windows packer (e.g. `"2048x2048"`).

use_raw_mouse.description:
Use the raw-input mouse API instead of the legacy WM_MOUSE messages. Improves
precision for high-DPI / high-polling-rate mice.

use_splash.description: Show the `splash_png` image before the first room loads.

Raw QOI, no outer compression.
PNG.
Pages ship inside the game data.
All of the group's pages live in external `.yytex` files, loaded together.

TextureLoadType.description: How the runtime loads a group's texture pages (yyp `loadType`).

border.description: Pixel gap added around each sprite frame in the packed texture page. Increase to prevent texture-bleeding artefacts at tile or sub-pixel boundaries.

mips.description: Number of mip levels to generate. `0` disables mipmaps entirely. `-1` lets the runtime choose the mip count automatically for the group. A positive value forces exactly that many mip levels.

scaled.description: Whether the runtime is allowed to scale this group's texture pages when applying resolution scaling.

autocrop.description: When `true`, the packer trims fully-transparent border pixels from each sprite frame before packing, reducing texture-page area. Disable if your game reads exact sprite-bbox coordinates.

parent.description: Name of a parent texture group whose settings are inherited when a field is omitted in this file. Optional; omit or leave empty for a standalone group.

compress_format.description: Texture compression for this group's pages. `bz2` stores bzip2-compressed QOI, `qoi` stores raw QOI, `png` stores PNG.

load_type.description: How the runtime loads this group's pages. `default` = inside the game data; `dynamic_group` / `dynamic_pages` store pages as external `.yytex` files loaded on demand (per group / per page).

texture_group.description:
Compile-time settings for one texture group (`texture_groups/<name>.toml`).
Sprites reference groups by name; the `default` group is used when no file is present.
texture_group.title: TextureGroup

streaming.description:
When `true`, sounds in this group are read from disk during playback rather
than bundled into the game package. Recommended for large music tracks.

export_dir.description:
Export directory for this audio group's external `.dat` file (the yyp
`GMAudioGroup.exportDir`). Empty = the project root. Preserved so the
AGRP chunk's external-filename paths survive the TOML round-trip.

targets.description:
Bitmask of GameMaker build targets this audio group is exported to
(the yyp `GMAudioGroup.targets` value). `-1` means
every platform. The WAD build zeroes the decoded `duration` of any
sound whose group does not target the platform being built, so this
value must survive the TOML round-trip to keep SOND parity.

audio_group.description:
Settings for an audio group asset. Audio groups let you load and unload
a set of sounds as a unit at runtime using `audio_group_load` / `audio_group_unload`.
audio_group.title: AudioGroup

Horizontally centred on the top edge.
Top-right corner.

SpriteOrigin.description:
Preset anchor point for a sprite's origin — the pixel used as the reference
for placement, rotation, and collision detection.
`custom` means the origin coordinates are specified explicitly with `origin_x`
and `origin_y`.

x.description: Horizontal offset of the origin in pixels from the left edge of the sprite.

y.description: Vertical offset of the origin in pixels from the top edge of the sprite.

CustomOrigin.description: Pixel coordinates of a custom origin point, measured from the sprite's top-left corner.

mode.description: How the bounding box is determined: `"automatic"`, `"full_image"`, or `"manual"`.

kind.description: Shape of the collision mask: `"rectangle"`, `"rotated_rectangle"`, `"ellipse"`, `"diamond"`, `"precise"`, or `"precise_per_frame"`.

tolerance.description: Alpha threshold (0–255) used for `"automatic"` bounding-box detection and `"precise"` mask generation; `0` means any non-fully-transparent pixel is included.

manual.description: Explicit bounding box coordinates. Required when `mode = "manual"`.

Collision.description: Collision mask configuration for the sprite.

oneOf.description: Bounding box is computed from the non-transparent pixels across all frames, using `tolerance` as the alpha threshold. Used when no `[collision]` block is present.
Bounding box covers the full sprite dimensions `(0, 0, width-1, height-1)`; no pixel sweep is performed.
Bounding box is taken verbatim from the `manual` rect; a `manual = { left, top, right, bottom }` block is required.

CollisionBboxMode.description: How the collision bounding box is determined. Corresponds to the three-mode menu in GameMaker's Sprite Editor.

oneOf.description: Axis-aligned rectangular mask. Fastest collision check.
Rectangular mask that rotates with the instance angle.
Elliptical mask fitted to the bounding box.
Diamond (rhombus) mask fitted to the bounding box.
Per-pixel precise mask merged across all frames. Accurate but slow.
Per-pixel precise mask computed separately for each animation frame.

Spine mesh mask — collision follows the deforming Spine skeleton.
Only valid for Spine (skeletal) sprites.

CollisionKind.description:
Shape used for a sprite's collision mask.
Simpler shapes are faster to evaluate; `precise` and `precise_per_frame`
check individual pixels and are the most accurate but most expensive.

left.description: Left edge of the collision rect (inclusive).

top.description: Top edge of the collision rect (inclusive).

right.description: Right edge of the collision rect (inclusive).

bottom.description: Bottom edge of the collision rect (inclusive).

ManualRect.description: Manually-specified collision bounding box. Required when `collision.mode = "manual"`. All coordinates are inclusive pixel offsets from the sprite's top-left corner.

enabled.description: When `false` the nine-slice guides are stored but not applied at runtime.

left.description: Pixel offset of the left guide from the sprite's left edge.

top.description: Pixel offset of the top guide from the sprite's top edge.

right.description: Pixel offset of the right guide from the sprite's right edge.

bottom.description: Pixel offset of the bottom guide from the sprite's bottom edge.

tile_mode.description: Scaling mode for each of the five regions, in order `[left, top, right, bottom, centre]`. Each is one of `"stretch"`, `"repeat"`, `"mirror"`, `"blank"`, or `"hide"`.

NineSlice.description: Nine-slice scaling configuration. Nine-slicing preserves corner and edge details when a sprite is scaled. See GameMaker's Nine Slice documentation for the guide layout.

NineSliceTileMode.description: One of "stretch", "repeat", "mirror", "blank", "hide" — or GameMaker's raw 0-4, which an older gmx wrote.

key.description: Timeline position (in playback units) at which this frame starts.

length.description: How many timeline units this frame occupies.

FrameKeyframe.description:
One frame keyframe on a sprite's built-in `frames` track. Controls
when a frame appears on the animation timeline and how long it is
held. The default timeline is `key = frame_index, length = 1`; only
sprites with variable-length / non-contiguous frame timing need to
carry these explicitly.

oneOf.description: Speed is expressed as real-world frames per second, independent of the room speed.
Speed is expressed as game frames per second, tied to the room's frame rate.

PlaybackSpeedType.description: How `playback_speed` is interpreted by the runtime.

key.description: Frame index (0-based) at which this event fires.

stretch.description: When `true`, the event is stretched to fill `length` frames.

disabled.description: When `true`, this event is ignored at runtime.

channels.description: Per-channel message lists fired by this keyframe.

SpriteEvent.description: One broadcast-message keyframe inside a sprite's sequence.

channel.description: Channel index for this event group; use `0` for standard broadcast messages.

events.description: List of message strings broadcast at this keyframe, receivable via the sequence `event_broadcast_message` handler.

SpriteEventChannel.description: One channel's broadcast messages within a keyframe.

SpineMeta.description:
Metadata for a Spine sprite that cannot be derived from the source
files: the sprite's authored pixel dimensions (the IDE preview-frame
size), which become the SPRT `width`/`height` and feed origin/bbox
derivation. The atlas page dimensions differ from these and are read
from the page PNGs at build time.

origin.description: Origin point used for placement, rotation, and `sprite_xoffset`/`sprite_yoffset`.

fps.description: Animation playback speed. Default: `30`. Units are controlled by `playback_speed_type`.

smooth.description: When `true`, GameMaker linearly interpolates between frames during playback.

texture_group.description: Texture group this sprite's frames are packed into; references `texture_groups/<name>.toml`.

custom_origin.description: Pixel coordinates of a custom origin point. Required when `origin = "custom"`, rejected otherwise.

collision.description: Collision mask configuration. Omit to use automatic bounding-box detection from frame pixels.

nine_slice.description: Nine-slice scaling configuration. Omit entirely to disable nine-slice for this sprite.

frame_ids.description: Optional list of UUIDs to use as frame identifiers instead of the default `frame_NNN` names. Leave empty for new sprites.

frame_durations.description:
Per-frame timeline keyframes for the built-in animation sequence,
in playback order. Each entry's `key`/`length` set when a frame
starts and how many timeline units it occupies. Leave empty for
the default 1-unit-per-frame, contiguous timeline (`key = i`,
`length = 1`); populate it only for variable-length / non-contiguous
timelines (e.g. a frame held for several steps).

h_tile.description: When `true`, the sprite tiles seamlessly in the horizontal direction.

v_tile.description: When `true`, the sprite tiles seamlessly in the vertical direction.

playback_speed_type.description: Unit for the `fps` value: `"frames_per_second"` or `"game_frames_per_second"` (for the latter, `fps` is a per-game-step `image_index` increment, not true FPS).

sequence_events.description: Broadcast-message keyframes for this sprite's built-in sequence (e.g. sound triggers at specific frames). Default: empty.

for_3d.description: When `true`, this sprite is placed on its own dedicated texture page rather than being atlas-packed, so 3D primitives can sample the full UV range.

pre_multiply_alpha.description: When `true`, frame pixels have RGB pre-multiplied by alpha at build time, which affects rendering under standard blend modes.

spine.description: Spine (skeletal-animation) sprite data. Present only for sprites imported from a Spine export; its presence marks this as a Spine sprite (GameMaker sprite `type: 2`). The skeleton `.json`, `.atlas`, and atlas page PNG(s) live alongside `sprite.toml`.

meta.description: Free-form metadata for tools and `::` references (`spr_x::meta.key`); the compiler ignores it.

sprite.description:
Sprite asset metadata. Frame images are read from sibling
`frame_NNN.png` (or `frame_NNN.jpg` / `frame_NNN.jpeg`) files, or a single
vector `frame_000.svg` (tessellated to a GameMaker vector shape at build).
sprite.title: Sprite

oneOf.description: Decoded PCM audio kept fully in memory. Zero-latency playback; best for short SFX.
Audio stored in compressed form in memory; decoded on each play. Saves RAM.
Audio decoded once at load time and kept in memory. Fastest repeated playback.
Audio read from disk during playback. Recommended for long music tracks.

CompressionMode.description:
Controls how a sound asset is stored and loaded at runtime.

Choose `uncompressed` for short sound effects that need zero-latency playback,
`compressed_load` to keep the asset compressed in memory (saves RAM, small decode
cost on each play), `decompress_load` to decode once on load (fastest playback,
highest memory use), or `streamed` to read the audio from disk during playback
(recommended for long music tracks that would otherwise occupy large amounts of RAM).

oneOf.description: Single-channel (mono) audio.

oneOf.description: Rectangular spawn region.
Elliptical spawn region.
Diamond-shaped spawn region.
Linear spawn region (a line segment).

ParticleShape.description:
Geometric shape of a particle emitter's spawn region.
Particles are created at positions within this shape.

oneOf.description: Uniform distribution — equal probability across the shape.
Normal (bell-curve) distribution — particles cluster toward the centre.
Inverted normal distribution — particles cluster toward the edges.

ParticleDistribution.description:
Probability distribution used when placing new particles within the
emitter shape.

x.description: X coordinate of the left edge of the spawn region.

y.description: Y coordinate of the top edge of the spawn region.

w.description: Width of the spawn region in pixels.

h.description: Height of the spawn region in pixels.

Region.description: Axis-aligned bounding box that defines where the emitter spawns particles in the room.

max.description: Maximum time value (inclusive). A random value between `min` and `max` is chosen each use.

TimedRange.description: A time range with explicit units, used for emission delay and interval.

oneOf.description: Time measured in game steps (frames). Value depends on the room speed.
Time measured in seconds, independent of room speed.

TimeUnits.description:
Time unit used for particle emitter timing values such as emission delay,
emission interval, and particle lifetime.

min.description: Minimum starting value; each particle picks a random value between `min` and `max` at spawn.

increase.description: Amount added to the value every step over the particle's lifetime (negative = decrease).

wiggle.description: Random amount added or subtracted each step (range -20 to 20).

Range.description: A numeric range with optional per-step drift and random wiggle, used for speed, direction, lifetime, and size.

direction.description: Direction of the gravitational pull in degrees (0 = right, 90 = up, 180 = left, 270 = down).

force.description: Strength of gravity added to particle speed per step (typically a small value such as `0.5`).

GravityVector.description: Constant acceleration applied to every particle of this emitter each step.

increase.description: Degrees added to the angle every step (negative = counter-clockwise).

wiggle.description: Random degrees added or subtracted each step (range -20 to 20).

relative.description: When `true`, the angle is relative to the particle's direction of travel; if speed reaches 0 the direction resets to 0° and the sprite will jump.

OrientationRange.description: Sprite rotation for particles, with optional per-step increase, wiggle, and direction-relative mode.

start.description: Colour at particle birth. Hex `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`. Default: empty (white).

mid.description: Colour at the midpoint of the particle's lifetime. Hex `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`. Default: empty (white).

end.description: Colour at particle death. Hex `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`. Default: empty (white).

ColourGradient.description: Three-stop colour gradient blended smoothly over each particle's lifetime (start → mid → end).

emitter.description: Name of the sibling emitter to trigger (the base name without the numeric prefix). Mutually exclusive with `preset`.

preset.description: Name of a built-in particle preset (a library emitter contributed by a forced prefab, e.g. `GM_Sparks`) to trigger instead of a sibling emitter. Mutually exclusive with `emitter`.

count.description: Number of particles to emit from the target emitter on each trigger.

SubSpawn.description: Reference to a sibling emitter that should be triggered as a sub-spawn.

shape.description: Shape of the spawn region. Determines where within `region` new particles appear.

distribution.description: Probability distribution for placing new particles within the region shape.

sprite.description: Sprite asset name to use for particles. Omit (or `null`) to use the built-in `shape` pixel types instead.

sprite_animate.description: When `true`, the sprite animates across its frames over each particle's lifetime.

sprite_stretch.description: When `true`, sprite animation is stretched to the particle's lifetime; otherwise it plays at the sprite's own speed.

sprite_random.description: When `true`, each particle starts on a random sprite frame.

texture.description:
Built-in particle texture index used when no custom `sprite` is set
(`GMPSEmitter.texture`). `7` is GameMaker's default round particle; `-1`
means no texture (e.g. an emitter that only triggers sub-spawn presets).
Ignored at build time when `sprite` is set (the sprite overrides it).

additive_blend.description: When `true`, particles are drawn with additive blending — overlapping particles brighten toward white, making dark colours nearly invisible.

region.description: Bounding box of the spawn region in room coordinates.

emit_count.description:
Number of particles emitted per burst interval.
`f32` to match GameMaker (`GMPSEmitter.emitCount` is a float and may be
negative).

emit_delay.description: Initial delay before the first emission, chosen randomly between `min` and `max`.

emit_interval.description: Time between consecutive bursts in stream mode, chosen randomly between `min` and `max`.

speed.description: Initial speed of each particle in pixels per step, with optional per-step increase and random wiggle.

direction.description: Initial direction of travel in degrees (0 = right, 90 = up, 180 = left, 270 = down), with optional per-step drift and wiggle.

gravity.description: Constant acceleration applied to every particle each step.

lifetime.description: Particle lifespan in steps (or seconds if `units` is `seconds`), chosen randomly between `min` and `max`.

size.description: Particle size as a scale multiplier relative to the sprite or built-in shape, with optional per-step growth and wiggle. Default multiplier `1.0` = original size.

orientation.description: Rotation of the particle sprite in degrees, with optional per-step increase and wiggle.

colours.description: Three-stop colour gradient applied over each particle's lifetime.

scale_x.description: Horizontal scale multiplier applied to the particle sprite/shape.

scale_y.description: Vertical scale multiplier applied to the particle sprite/shape.

spawn_on_death.description: Sub-emitter to trigger once when a particle reaches the end of its lifetime.

spawn_on_update.description: Sub-emitter to trigger every step for each live particle.

emitter.description:
One particle emitter — `emitters/<NN>_<name>.toml`.
The numeric prefix in the filename sets the emitter's evaluation order; the bare `<name>` is used by sub-spawn references.
emitter.title: Emitter

width.description: Width of one tile in pixels.

height.description: Height of one tile in pixels.

TileSize.description: Width and height of a single tile in the grid, in pixels.

h.description: Horizontal separation per tile side, in pixels.

v.description: Vertical separation per tile side, in pixels.

TileSeparation.description:
Pixel gap between tiles in the source sprite sheet.
Per `tileset_get_info`, the space between two adjacent tiles is `2 × separator` (one on each side).

x.description: Horizontal offset of the tile grid origin, in pixels.

y.description: Vertical offset of the tile grid origin, in pixels.

TileOffset.description: Pixel offset of the first tile from the top-left corner of the sprite sheet.

name.description: Identifier for this animation cycle.

fps.description: Playback speed in frames per second.

frames.description: Ordered list of tile grid indices that make up the animation frames.

TileAnimation.description:
A named animation cycle: a sequence of tile indices played at a given frame rate.
Indices refer to positions in the tile grid (0 = top-left, left-to-right, top-to-bottom).

name.description: Identifier for this brush.

width.description: Width of the brush in tiles (number of columns).

height.description: Height of the brush in tiles (number of rows).

tiles.description:
Row-major tile indices, one inner array per row of `width` cells.
Indices are 0-based into the tile grid; `0` marks an empty cell (no
tile), matching the tilemap convention.

transforms.description:
Per-tile transform overrides (flip / rotate) for the brush's cells.
Omit or leave empty when no tile in the brush needs flipping or
rotation. Uses the same encoding as the `Indices` tile-map form.

origin.description:
Editor-only anchor: the brush editor working-grid cell where the brush's
top-left tile sits. `tiles`/`width`/`height` are minimized to the
content's bounding box and carry no position of their own, so this lets
the editor restore the brush to where it was painted. Like the rest of
the brush it is stripped at compile time.

TileBrush.description:
A custom tile brush: a named rectangular arrangement of tiles that the
editor stamps as a single unit, acting as a palette of commonly grouped
tiles (GameMaker's "custom brush" feature).

Brushes are pure authoring metadata. The compiler never reads them, so
they are stripped from the compiled game — they exist only to make level
authoring in the editor faster.

col.description: Column (0-based) of the brush's top-left tile on the editor grid.

row.description: Row (0-based) of the brush's top-left tile on the editor grid.

BrushOrigin.description:
Working-grid anchor for a [`TileBrush`] in the tileset brush editor: the cell
its top-left tile occupies. Pure editor authoring metadata.

template.description: Which of GameMaker's two auto-tile templates this set uses. Decides the mask vocabulary and how a `shape` is read.

fill.description: Tile drawn under empty (`.`) cells. Omit to leave empty cells blank.

network.description: `true` for connectivity networks (rails, fences, pipes) where diagonals carry no meaning and only the four sides matter.

edges.description: Default out-of-bounds behaviour per side; a layer's own `[autotile].edges` overrides it.

tiles.description: Mask key → the tile index, or a list of interchangeable variants picked per cell.

AutotileSet.description:
One auto-tile set: a table mapping each neighbour-mask a tile layer can need onto the tile index (or indices) that draw it.
`template` decides the mask vocabulary — `sides_47` keys look like `"NESW|NE,NW"` / `"ES|"` / `"|"`, `corners_16` keys look like `"NE+NW"` / `"-"`.
Partial tables are normal: 14-tile sets, 16-mask subsets, and connectivity networks all cover less than the full 47.

oneOf.description: GameMaker's 47-tile template: sides plus relevant diagonals. The default, and what platformer / side-on terrain uses.
GameMaker's 16-tile template: a corner (Wang) set. Recommended for top-down landscapes, where corners give smoother diagonal joins.

AutotileTemplate.description:
Which of GameMaker's two auto-tile templates a set uses.
`sides_47` keys a tile by which of its four sides connect (plus the diagonals those make relevant); `corners_16` keys it by which of its four corners carry terrain.
A `corners_16` set reads its `shape` as the lattice *between* tiles, so the generated map is one cell smaller on each axis.

anyOf.description: Interchangeable tile indices, all drawing the same mask.

TileVariants.description: One tile index, or several interchangeable ones. With a list, `apply` picks per cell from a hash of the cell's position and the layer's `seed`, so the choice is stable under edits elsewhere in the shape.

sprite.description:
Name of the sprite asset used as the tile sheet. `None` when the
tileset has no backing sprite (`spriteId: null` in the yyp); the
BGND entry then carries `sprite_index = -1` and packs no texture.

tile_size.description: Width and height of each tile, in pixels. Required.

separation.description: Gap between tiles in the source sheet. Defaults to zero on all sides.

offset.description: Pixel offset of the tile grid from the top-left of the source sheet. Defaults to zero.

output_columns.description: Number of tile columns in the **packed output atlas** GameMaker builds, not the source sheet's grid — the two rarely match. Omit to let the compiler choose. For the sheet's real grid run `gmx tools tileset-info`, which reads it from the image.

output_border.description: Pixel border added around the tile atlas page.

tile_count.description: Total number of tiles in the source sheet's grid (rows × columns). Required for animated tilesets so the runtime knows the animation frame layout.

animation_speed.description: Playback speed for tile animations in frames per second.

frame_data.description:
Flat list of tile indices describing every animation frame for every animated tile, in tile-index order.
Leave empty for a non-animated tileset; supply a flat sequence of `frame_count` indices per tile for animated tilesets.

animations.description: Optional named animation cycles for authoring convenience. Each entry names a subset of `frame_data` by tile index range.

brushes.description: Custom tile brushes: named rectangular groups of tiles that stamp as a unit, mirroring GameMaker's custom-brush palette. Pure authoring metadata — brushes are editor-only and are stripped at compile time, never reaching the runtime game.

sprite_no_export.description: When `true`, the backing sprite is excluded from the standalone sprite list and will not appear as an independent sprite asset at runtime; the tileset itself is still usable.

texture_group.description: Texture group that the tile atlas is packed into.

autotile.description:
Named auto-tile sets, each a neighbour-mask → tile-index table, letting a `kind = "tiles"` layer be authored as terrain — a block of `#`/`.` — instead of hand-picked indices.
One tileset may carry several, exactly as GameMaker's Tile Set Editor allows; a layer picks one with `[autotile].set`.
Build one with `gmx autotile derive <tileset>`; see `gmx docs lookup autotile --category gmx` for the mask-key grammar.

step.description:
Frame (step) at which this moment fires, counting from the start of the
timeline. Moments are typically authored in ascending `step` order.

code.description: GML executed when the timeline reaches `step`. May be empty.

Moment.description: A single moment within a timeline: a frame number plus the GML run there.

moments.description:
Ordered moments that make up this timeline. May be empty (a blank
timeline). Each moment fires once when the timeline position reaches
its `step`.

timeline.description:
A timeline asset — a sequence of moments. Each moment runs its GML code
when the timeline reaches the moment's `step` (frame). Attach a timeline
to an instance with `timeline_index` + `timeline_running` to drive
scripted, frame-based behaviour.
timeline.title: Timeline

RigView.description:
The named views a rig's art can be authored for. Yaw/pitch in degrees:
side = (90, 0) — the character's RIGHT profile; side_left =
(-90, 0), the left profile, for asymmetric characters that cannot just
mirror; front = (0, 0); back = (180, 0); the four isometric diagonals =
(±45/±135, 30).

name.description:
Unique name for this attachment within the rig. Referenced by
`draw_order` and, at runtime, by
`rig_set_attachment_sprite`/`rig_set_attachment_visible`.

sprite.description:
Sprite asset this attachment draws, by name (e.g.
`"spr_ballet_skirt"`). Resolved and validated at build time.

bone.description:
Bone this attachment is rigidly parented to. Any bone name on the
rig's chain path (e.g. `"mixamorig:Hips"`).

at.description: Placement origin, in atlas pixel coordinates.

angle.description: Rotation offset in degrees, relative to the bone.

visible.description:
Whether this attachment is drawn by default. Defaults to `true`;
toggled per-instance via `rig_set_attachment_visible(rig, name, visible)`.

Attachment.description:
One sprite attached to a rig at a specific bone (`[[attachment]]` in
`rig.toml`).

body.description: Segments that get a body of their own, parents before children.

rider.description: Segments with no body of their own, rigidly carried by one that has.

Ragdoll.description:
A rig's ragdoll layout. Authored per rig, so a skeleton and a heavyset man
need not share one set of joint limits.

bone.description: The bone leading the drawn segment this body stands in for.

parent.description:
The body this one hinges on. Empty for the root (typically the hips),
which has no joint. Must appear earlier in the list.

limit.description:
The joint's ANATOMICAL range in degrees, `[lo, hi]`: the child
segment's direction relative to its parent's, NOT an offset from the
bind pose. Straight is 0, and a hinge that bends one way gets a
near-zero bound on the other. The range must contain 0.

Stated for the unmirrored character; the runtime flips and swaps the
pair when the rig faces the other way.

width.description:
The collision box's width in px at the rig's authored scale. Keep it
near the drawn art's thickness so a body resting on the floor does not
sink through it.

reference.description:
Where the joint's neutral sits relative to the parent: `0` for hinges
that continue in line (elbow, knee, ankle, neck), `180` for limbs that
hang opposite the torso (shoulder, hip). Without it those sit exactly
on the +/-180 wrap, where no limit means anything. Defaults to `0`.

extend.description:
A bone whose tail the box reaches to, for a segment whose art carries
on past it — a forearm's box ends at the fingertips rather than the
wrist. The segment still DRAWS at its own length; only the box is
longer. Empty (the default) stops at this segment's own tail.

motor.description:
Scales this joint's straightening torque. Arms want far less than
legs: a corpse's legs hold roughly straight under their own stiffness
while the arms should hang and drag. Defaults to `1.0`.

RagdollBody.description:
One ragdoll body: the box it collides as, and how its joint to the parent
behaves.

bone.description: The bone leading the carried segment.

RagdollRider.description:
A segment with no body of its own, carried rigidly by one that has — a
hand on its forearm, a neck on the hips.

atlas.description:
The SPRITE this rig's meshes are textured from, by asset name (e.g.
`"spr_droid_atlas"`). Mesh vertices in `rig.json` are pixel
coordinates in this image, so the sprite must be authored
`for_3d = true` (a texture page of its own) — lacking the flag is a
build error. Baked into the RIG blob; `rig_set_atlas` overrides per
instance. Empty leaves the atlas unresolved and the
rig draws only if GML supplies one.

view.description:
The view this rig's atlas was drawn for; the runtime projects every
clip at it. One rig asset per authored direction. Defaults to `side`.

draw_order.description:
Back-to-front draw order: one list spanning both body chains (by
`chains[].name` in `rig.json`) and attachments (by
`[[attachment]].name`). Required of every rig that has any layer,
and it must place every one exactly once — a missing list or a
left-out layer is a load error rather than an invisible layer.

attachment.description:
Sprites layered onto the rig at specific bones — a shield, a skirt,
hair. Ordinary SPRITE assets; only their placement on this rig
lives here.

preserve_joints.description:
Skinning at the joints: a mesh vertex weighted between two bones that
meet at a joint rotates about that joint by its share of the bend,
keeping its distance from it, instead of averaging the two bones'
transforms (which pinches knees and elbows at deep bends). Auto-rig
turns it on; off is plain linear blending.

plane_lock.description:
**Ignored** — plane lock is derived from [`Rig::view`] at bake
([`RigView::corrections`]). Accepted so older `rig.toml` files still
parse under `deny_unknown_fields`.

anti_twist.description:
Correction, 0..1: how far a limb chain's root moves toward the socket
the parent bone's 2D frame implies, so body twist doesn't slide the
arm across a flat chest. Defaults to `1.0`; also accepts
`true`/`false` (1.0 / 0.0). Baked into the RIG blob as-is.

ragdoll.description:
The ragdoll's collision layout: one box per drawn segment that gets a
physics body, plus the finer segments that ride one. Optional — a rig
with none simply cannot be ragdolled. The boxes are also readable from
GML (`rig_body_box`, `rig_body_point_distance`) for hit testing,
whether or not a doll is running.

still_hands.description:
Correction, 0..1: how far the hand segments are held at their bind
pose relative to the forearm, so finger animation a flat drawn hand
cannot express doesn't read as wobble. Defaults to `1.0`; also
accepts `true`/`false` (1.0 / 0.0). Baked into the RIG blob as-is.

rig.description:
A Rig asset (`rigs/<name>/`): an atlas image plus deforming meshes
bound to bones. Free-standing from any particular clip — any CLIP
whose bone topology matches can drive it (checked at compile time).
rig.title: Rig

name.description:
The name GML sees. Several markers may share one name; seeking
functions take the first by time.

ClipMarker.description:
One `[[marker]]`: a named time in the clip, in seconds. `at` past the
clip's duration is a load error.

marker.description:
Named moments in this clip's local time — footsteps, hit frames —
surfaced to GML by `rig_poll_markers` as playback crosses them, and
the targets of `rig_goto_marker` / `rig_play_to_marker`.

clip.description:
A Clip asset: one baked skeletal animation (`clips/<name>/`). The
keyframe data lives in the sibling `clip.json`; `clip.toml` carries the
authored layer on top: the markers.
clip.title: Clip
